title: Coastal management methods table
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y8 lesson 7 (Coastal management methods table (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 7: Happisburgh and protecting places from the sea; unit quiz (4.7, 4.8). To understand how coasts are managed and why some places, like Happisburgh, are not fully protected

questions.q: Give two reasons Happisburgh erodes fast.
questions.a: Soft sand and clay cliffs; powerful North Sea storm waves; broken old defences
questions.model: Think: rock and waves. Rock: soft sand and clay. Waves: strong North Sea storms. So the cliffs erode fast.

questions.a: They starve beaches further along the coast of sand
Letting the sea erode or flood an area in a planned way

questions.q: Core: Coasts unit quiz on the portal (12 questions: waves, tides, erosion, longshore drift, landforms, uses, management).
questions.a: Answers in the portal quiz key
questions.model: Teacher does question 1 aloud: 'What is fetch?' The distance of open water the wind blows over.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box: 'Happisburgh should be protected.' Do you agree? Give both sides and a judgement.
questions.a: Balanced answer using cost, fairness to residents and effects on other coasts, ending with a reasoned judgement

questions.q: Stretch: Why does a shoreline management plan look at a whole stretch of coast, not one village?
questions.a: Defences in one place affect sediment and erosion elsewhere along the coast

questions.q: Big question: should we protect every home from the sea?
questions.a: Reasoned view: not always, because of cost and effects elsewhere, but people affected should be treated fairly
